title: NTA UGC NET English Full Mock Test #06
subtitle: 100 Questions · 200 Marks · Post-2018 NTA Pattern · Zero Answer Bias (25 A/B/C/D) · Reading Comprehension (Q91-100)

items.title: Mock #06 · Q1
items.stem:
Match the character with the work :
I.
Count Fosco
A.
Villette
II.
Margaret
B.
Adam Bede
III.
Lucy Snowe
C.
The Woman in White
IV.
Maggie Tulliver
D.
North or South

Codes :

I
II
III
IV
items.explanation: Count Fosco (I) is the suave villain of Wilkie Collins's The Woman in White (1859–60, C); Margaret Hale (II) is the heroine of Elizabeth Gaskell's North and South (1854–55, D); Lucy Snowe (III) is the narrator-protagonist of Charlotte Brontë's Villette (1853, A); and Maggie Tulliver (IV) is paired with fellow George Eliot novel Adam Bede (B), giving C-D-A-B.

items.title: Mock #06 · Q2
items.stem: Which of the following is an accurate description of 'heteroglossia' ?
options: Heteroglossia makes the job of the novelist easier by incorporating diversity into the novelistic structure
Heteroglossia enters the linguistic universe of the novel to homogenize its multiple differences and voices in a singular vision of accomplished structure
Heteroglossia creates concrete conceptualisations through language in association with the singular view of the artistic effort resulting in the unified world of the novel
Heteroglossia functions in a novel in alliance with its stylistic system incorporating multiple voices inscribed in social language and differentiated components of a writer's ideological position
items.explanation: Coined by Russian theorist Mikhail Bakhtin in 'Discourse in the Novel' (1934–35), 'heteroglossia' (raznorechie) refers to the coexistence of multiple social voices, registers, and ideological perspectives orchestrated within the stylistic system of the novel.

items.title: Mock #06 · Q3
items.stem:
Joseph Addison was associated with which of the following?

A. The London Magazine
B. The Spectator
C. The Gentleman's Magazine
D. The Tatler
E. The Rambler

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Joseph Addison was a major contributor to Richard Steele's The Tatler (1709–1711, D) and co-founded with Steele the celebrated daily periodical The Spectator (1711–1712, 1714, B).

items.title: Mock #06 · Q4
items.stem:
The world dominated by cold and
hypocritical materialists is represented
by William Blake in the mythological
figure of __________
items.explanation: In William Blake's prophetic mythology (such as The Book of Urizen, 1794), Urizen ('Your Reason') is the tyrannical, bearded figure who embodies cold Enlightenment rationalism, restrictive moral law, and hypocritical materialism.

items.title: Mock #06 · Q5
items.stem:
Arrange the following in order of their publication:
A. Religio Medici
B. The Terrors of the Night
C. Essays of Elia
D. Utopia
E. The Four Ages of Poetry
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: The chronological order of publication is: Thomas More's Utopia (1516, D), Thomas Nashe's The Terrors of the Night (1594, B), Sir Thomas Browne's Religio Medici (1642/1643, A), Thomas Love Peacock's The Four Ages of Poetry (1820, E), and Charles Lamb's Essays of Elia (1823, C).

items.title: Mock #06 · Q6
items.stem:
Wallace Stevens' "The Man with the Blue Guitar" may be linked to the work of the
following artist
items.explanation: Wallace Stevens's modernist poem 'The Man with the Blue Guitar' (1937), which meditates on the relationship between artistic imagination and reality ('things as they are'), was inspired by Pablo Picasso's 1903–1904 Blue Period painting The Old Guitarist.

items.title: Mock #06 · Q7
items.stem:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I: The teaching of non-native literature to the students of English Language Teaching is arid.
Statement II: The negative responses in ELT classroom can create an interesting classroom situation.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
items.explanation: Teaching non-native and postcolonial literatures in English Language Teaching (ELT) classrooms enriches intercultural competence rather than being arid (Statement I is incorrect), while learners' critical or negative responses can stimulate productive classroom debate (Statement II is correct).

items.title: Mock #06 · Q8
items.stem:
From among the following, identify Coleridge's companion in a fanciful scheme to
establish a Utopian community of free love on the banks of the Susquehaina river ?
items.explanation: In 1794, Samuel Taylor Coleridge and fellow Romantic poet Robert Southey devised "Pantisocracy," an idealistic utopian scheme to establish an egalitarian commune on the banks of the Susquehanna River in Pennsylvania.

items.title: Mock #06 · Q9
items.stem:
Kimberle Crenshaw's term "intersectionality" is widely used for
A. academic deterioration
B. racial justice
C. peace formation
D. complex construction of power
E. identity politics
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
items.explanation: Legal scholar Kimberlé Crenshaw coined the term 'intersectionality' (1989) to analyze how overlapping social categorizations such as race, gender, and class create interlocking systems of discrimination and privilege, making it central to racial justice (B), the complex construction of power (D), and identity politics (E).

items.title: Mock #06 · Q10
items.stem: Functional Communicative Approach in English Language Teaching is in opposition to
items.explanation: In English Language Teaching (ELT), the Functional-Communicative Approach arose in direct opposition to the Structural Approach: whereas the Structural Approach drills isolated grammatical structures and sentence patterns, the Communicative Approach prioritizes real-life social functions and meaningful interaction.

items.title: Mock #06 · Q11
items.stem:
Match the author with the title :
(Author) (Title)
(a) Alan Paton  (i) Open City
(b) Ngugi wa Thiong’o  (ii) Cry, the Beloved Country
(c) Teju Cole  (iii) A Grain of Wheat
(d) Wole Soyinka  (iv) The Interpreters
items.explanation: Paton wrote Cry, the Beloved Country, Ngugi A Grain of Wheat, Teju Cole Open City, and Soyinka The Interpreters.

items.title: Mock #06 · Q12
items.stem: Which among the following is not a character from Jane Austen's novel Persuasion?
items.explanation: Mary Crawford is a fashionable, worldly character in Jane Austen's Mansfield Park (1814), whereas Sir Walter Elliot, Lady Russell, and Captain Frederick Wentworth are central characters in Persuasion (1818).

items.title: Mock #06 · Q13
items.stem:
Which of the following statements are correct?
A. The term 'performativity' was coined by Derrida
B. The idea of 'meme' was originally coined by Richard Dawkings.
C. The term 'The culture industry' was coined by Adorno and Horkheimer.
D. The term 'Ideological State Apparatus' was coined by Bakhtin
E. The term 'Womanism' was coined by Alice Walker.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below
items.explanation: Evolutionary biologist Richard Dawkins coined the term 'meme' in The Selfish Gene (1976, B), Theodor Adorno and Max Horkheimer coined 'the culture industry' in Dialectic of Enlightenment (1947, C), and Alice Walker coined 'Womanism' in In Search of Our Mothers' Gardens (1983, E). 'Performativity' was developed by J. L. Austin and Judith Butler, and 'Ideological State Apparatus' by Louis Althusser; thus B, C, E only.

items.title: Mock #06 · Q14
items.stem: According to Jeremy Hawthorn, which of the following can be said to "have prepared the ground for the development of theories of the gaze"?
options: Michael Argyle and Mark Cook's Gaze and Mutual Gaze
Sigmund Freud's Three Essays on the Theory of Sexuality
Michel Foucault's Discipline and Punish: The Birth of the Prison
items.explanation: In A Glossary of Contemporary Literary Theory, Jeremy Hawthorn observes that John Berger's Ways of Seeing (1972) prepared the ground for feminist and film theories of the gaze by showing how men look at women while women watch themselves being looked at.

items.title: Mock #06 · Q15
items.stem:
Arrange the following characters in the chronological order in which they appeared in Indian literature.
 A. Praneshacharya (Samskara)
 B. Sakuni (Mahabharata)
 C. Rusty (The Room on the Roof)
 D. Gobar (Godan)
 Choose the correct answer from the options given below
items.explanation: These characters appeared in Indian literature in the chronological order: Shakuni in Vyasa's ancient Sanskrit epic Mahabharata (B), Gobar in Munshi Premchand's Hindi novel Godaan (1936, D), Rusty in Ruskin Bond's The Room on the Roof (1956, C), and Praneshacharya in U.R. Ananthamurthy's Kannada novel Samskara (1965, A).

items.title: Mock #06 · Q16
items.stem:
[Reading Comprehension: Poem]
Read the following poem carefully and answer the questions that follow:

"Leaning into the afternoons I cast my sad nets
towards your oceanic eyes.
There in the highest blaze my solitude lengthens and flames
its arms turning like a drowning man's.
I send out red signals across your absent eyes
that smell like the sea or the beach by a lighthouse.
You keep only darkness, my distant female,
from your regard sometimes the coast of dread emerges.
Leaning into the afternoons I fling my sad nets
to that sea that is thrashed by your oceanic eyes."
— Pablo Neruda

Question:
What is the central theme of the poem?
items.explanation: The entire poem centers on the speaker's yearning toward an emotionally detached lover ('my distant female'), making unrequited love and deep longing the core thematic focus.

items.title: Mock #06 · Q17
items.stem:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Derrida mentions that an aesthetic discourse always involves values and interests, independent from "a pure and neutral aesthetic realm".
Statement II: Derrida believed that the outside influence in assessment of aesthetics always enters as and when philosophers and historians point out the element of "truth".

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
items.explanation: In The Truth in Painting (La Vérité en peinture, 1978), Jacques Derrida deconstructs the Kantian 'parergon' (frame), demonstrating that aesthetic discourse is never a pure, autonomous realm detached from extrinsic values and interests (Statement I is correct) and that philosophical and historical claims about 'truth' continually traverse the boundary between inside and outside in aesthetic judgment (Statement II is correct).

items.title: Mock #06 · Q18
items.stem:
“Yet it is the masculine values that prevail”, observed a famous writer “Speaking cruelly”,
she continued, “football and sport are ‘important’, the worship of fashion, the buying of
clothes ‘trivial’.”
Name the author and the text.
options: Virginia Woolf, A Room of One’s Own
Mary Wollstonecraft, A Vindication of the Rights of Woman
Jean Rhys, After Leaving Mr. Mackenzie
items.explanation: In Chapter 4 of A Room of One's Own (1929), Virginia Woolf observes the pervasive gendered hierarchy of cultural valuation: 'Speaking cruelly, football and sport are "important"; the worship of fashion, the buying of clothes "trivial". And these values are inevitably transferred from life to fiction.'

items.title: Mock #06 · Q19
items.stem:
Which two works in the following list are written by Aphra Behn?
A. Rover
B. Oroonoko
C. Soldier's Fortune
D. The Princess of Cleve
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Restoration writer Aphra Behn wrote the comedy The Rover (1677, A) and the prose novella Oroonoko: or, The Royal Slave (1688, B), whereas The Soldier's Fortune is by Thomas Otway and The Princess of Cleves by Madame de La Fayette (and dramatized by Nathaniel Lee).

items.title: Mock #06 · Q20
items.stem: In his essay “The Function of Criticism at the Present Time” (1864) Matthew Arnold contended that
options: Critical power should be ranked higher than creative power
Creative power should be ranked higher than critical power
Creative and critical powers should be ranked equally
Creative and critical powers are not comparable in any way
items.explanation: Arnold says the creative power is higher than the critical, but criticism prepares the ground for great creative work.

items.title: Mock #06 · Q21
items.stem:
Match the titles of the following poems by Tennyson with their opening lines according to the code given below :
List – I (Titles of poems)
(i) 'Tithonus'
(ii) 'The Lotos-Eaters'
(iii) 'Ulysses'
(iv) 'The Lady of Shalott'

List – II (Opening Lines)
(1) “Courage” he said, and pointed towards the land. The mounting wave will roll us shoreward soon.
(2) “The woods decay, the woods decay and fall, The vapours weep their burthen to the ground.”
(3) “On either side the river lie Long fields of barley and of rye.”
(4) “It little profits that an idle king, By this still hearth, among these barren crags, Matched with an aged wife, I mete and dole Unequal laws unto a savage race.”

Codes : (i) (ii) (iii) (iv)
items.explanation: Tennyson's 'Tithonus' opens with 'The woods decay, the woods decay and fall' (2), 'The Lotos-Eaters' with '"Courage!" he said, and pointed toward the land' (1), 'Ulysses' with 'It little profits that an idle king' (4), and 'The Lady of Shalott' with 'On either side the river lie' (3).

items.title: Mock #06 · Q22
items.stem: "To Daffodils" is a poem, written by
items.explanation: 'To Daffodils' ('Fair Daffodils, we weep to see / You haste away so soon') is a lyric poem on the brevity of human life by Cavalier poet Robert Herrick, published in his collection Hesperides (1648).

items.title: Mock #06 · Q23
items.stem:
Which two of the following are autobiographical narratives?
(a) Kanthapura
(b) Meatless Days
(c) Prison and Chocolate Cake
(d) The God of Small Things
The correct option is :
items.explanation: Sara Suleri's Meatless Days (b, 1989) and Nayantara Sahgal's Prison and Chocolate Cake (c, 1954) are memoirs/autobiographical narratives, whereas Raja Rao's Kanthapura and Arundhati Roy's The God of Small Things are novels.

items.title: Mock #06 · Q24
items.stem: Identify the correctly matched group
options: Third Space - Edward Soja Hybridity - Homi Bhabha Reception aesthetics - Wolfgang Iser Langue - Ferdinand de Saussure
Third Space - Ernst Bloch Hybridity - Edward Said Reception aesthetics - Eve K. Sedgwick Langue - G. S. Frazer
Third Space - Wolfgang Iser Hybridity - Edward Soja Reception aesthetics - Ferdinand de Saussure Langue - Homi Bhabha
Third Space - G. S. Frazer Hybridity - Eve K. Sedgwick Reception aesthetics - Edward Soja Langue - Edward Said
items.explanation: The correctly matched theoretical concepts and thinkers are: 'Third Space' (Thirdspace) with postmodern geographer Edward Soja, 'Hybridity' with postcolonial theorist Homi K. Bhabha, 'Reception aesthetics' with Constance School critic Wolfgang Iser, and 'Langue' with structuralist linguist Ferdinand de Saussure.

items.title: Mock #06 · Q25
items.stem: Identify the right chronological sequence
options: The American Pastoral - Sister Carrie - The Great Gatsby - Beloved
Sister Carrie - The Great Gatsby - Beloved - The American Pastoral
The Great Gatsby - Sister Carrie - Beloved - The American Pastoral
Sister Carrie - The Great Gatsby - The American Pastoral - Beloved
items.explanation: The correct chronological order of these American novels is Theodore Dreiser's Sister Carrie (1900), F. Scott Fitzgerald's The Great Gatsby (1925), Toni Morrison's Beloved (1987), and Philip Roth's American Pastoral (1997).

items.title: Mock #06 · Q26
items.stem:
In the opening pages of one of Thomas Mann's novels we can see space itself becoming a
form of time : "Space, like time, engenders forgetfulness but it does so by setting us
bodily free from our surroundings and giving us back our primitive unattached state."
Which is the novel ?
items.explanation: This reflection on how travel through space, like time, induces forgetfulness appears in the opening chapter ('Arrival') of Thomas Mann's philosophical novel The Magic Mountain (Der Zauberberg, 1924), as young Hans Castorp journeys by train up into the Swiss Alps to visit his cousin at the Berghof sanatorium.

items.title: Mock #06 · Q27
items.meta: Unit IX: Literary Theory Post World War II
items.stem: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Toni Morrison and Adrienne Rich have contributed to a distinctive style. Reason (R): Feminism, Adrienne Rich observes, is the field where "subjectivity and politics have to come together" in the most natural way. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
items.explanation: Both statements are factually correct: Toni Morrison and Adrienne Rich each created a distinctive aesthetic style in American literature, and Adrienne Rich observed in her feminist essays that subjectivity and politics unite in feminism. However, Rich's theoretical comment on feminist methodology does not explain why both writers evolved their specific stylistic signatures, so Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

items.title: Mock #06 · Q28
items.stem: According to Northrop Frye there are four main narrative genres associated with the seasonal cycle of spring, summer, autumn and winter. They are comedy, ________, tragedy and irony (satire). Which is the second one ?
items.explanation: In Anatomy of Criticism (1957), Northrop Frye maps the four mythoi (narrative genres) onto the four seasons: Comedy (Spring), Romance (Summer), Tragedy (Autumn), and Irony/Satire (Winter).

items.title: Mock #06 · Q29
items.stem:
Which of the following writers do not exclusively belong to the eighteenth century ?
(A) Oliver Goldsmith
(B) Thomas Gray
(C) Robert Southey
(D) William Cowper
(E) Charles Lamb
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Oliver Goldsmith (1728–1774), Thomas Gray (1716–1771), and William Cowper (1731–1800) lived and wrote in the eighteenth century, whereas Romantic poet Robert Southey (1774–1843, C) and essayist Charles Lamb (1775–1834, E) flourished in the nineteenth century; thus (C) and (E) Only.

items.title: Mock #06 · Q30
items.meta: Unit V: Language: Basic Concepts, Theories and Pedagogy
items.stem: The Grammar Translation Method in English Language Teaching stresses on:
items.explanation: The Grammar Translation Method focuses on prescriptive grammatical rules, rote vocabulary memorization, and word-for-word translation between the native and target languages. As a result, it prioritizes strict grammatical accuracy over oral fluency or communicative appropriateness.

items.title: Mock #06 · Q31
items.stem:
Match the following :
(Statements on Imagination) — (Poets / Critics)
I. "One power alone makes a poet – The Imagination, The Divine Vision" — 1. Shelley
II. "… what the imagination seizes on beauty must be the truth" — 2. Coleridge
III. "The great instrument of moral good is the imagination" — 3. Blake
IV. "Works of imagination should be written in a very plain language" — 4. Keats
The right combination according to the code is :
Code : I II III IV
items.explanation: 'One Power alone makes a Poet: Imagination, The Divine Vision' is by William Blake (annotations to Wordsworth) (I-3); 'What the imagination seizes as Beauty must be truth' is from John Keats's letter to Benjamin Bailey (Nov 22, 1817) (II-4); 'The great instrument of moral good is the imagination' is from P.B. Shelley's A Defence of Poetry (III-1); and 'Works of imagination should be written in very plain language' is from S.T. Coleridge's Table Talk (IV-2).

items.title: Mock #06 · Q32
items.stem: In Eliot's Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock who among the following painters is the subject of conversation among the perambulating women?
items.explanation: The refrain 'In the room the women come and go / Talking of Michelangelo' refers to Michelangelo.

items.title: Mock #06 · Q33
items.stem:
Which of the following statement(s) are true about “Synecdoche” ?
(A) It is a comparison between two objects
(B) It is a figure of speech in which part refers to the whole
(C) It is a figure of speech in which the name of an attribute is substituted for that of the thing meant
(D) It is a comparison between two unrelated objects
(E) It is a figure of speech in which the whole refers to a part
items.explanation: Synecdoche is a figure of speech in which a part refers to the whole (B), such as 'new wheels' for a car, or the whole refers to a part (E), such as 'society' for high society. Statement C describes metonymy, while A and D refer to similes or metaphors.

items.title: Mock #06 · Q34
items.stem:
An Indian English poet once remarked that his discipline and education ave him his “outer”
hereas his Indian origin ave him “inner” form. Reflecting a part of this claim is a famous
essay he called __________ .
options: “Is There a Native Way of Thinking ?”
“Is There an Indian Way of Thinking ?”
“Where Do We Go from Here : Some Speculations”
items.explanation: In his celebrated essay 'Is There an Indian Way of Thinking? An Informal Essay' (1989), scholar and poet A. K. Ramanujan analyzed how his Western academic training gave him his 'outer' cognitive framework while his native Indian upbringing provided his 'inner' cultural sensibility.

items.title: Mock #06 · Q35
items.stem:
Arrange the following texts in the chronological order of publication.
A. This Bridge Called My Back
B. Sexual Politics
C. Gender Trouble
D. The Feminine Mystique

Choose the correct answer from the options given below
items.explanation: The chronological order of these landmark feminist works is Betty Friedan's The Feminine Mystique (1963, D), Kate Millett's Sexual Politics (1970, B), Cherríe Moraga and Gloria Anzaldúa's This Bridge Called My Back (1981, A), and Judith Butler's Gender Trouble (1990, C).

items.title: Mock #06 · Q36
items.stem: Women of Palestine (1982) and Indian Women in Struggle (1980) deal with :
options: women's struggle at their work place
items.explanation: Ingela Bendt and James Downing's We Shall Return: Women of Palestine (1982) and Gail Omvedt's We Will Smash This Prison! Indian Women in Struggle (1980) document grassroots female militancy, anti-colonial resistance, and political mobilization.

items.title: Mock #06 · Q37
items.stem:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The Orientalists in British India were not sympathetic towards India's ancient
learning.

Statement II: William Jones thought that in "imagination", "ratiocination", and philosophy,
Indians were by no means inferior to Europeans.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Statement | is incorrect but Statement II is true
Both Statement | and Statement II are false
Statement | is correct but Statement II is false
Both Statement | and Statement Il are true
items.explanation: Statement I is false because British Orientalist scholars—such as Warren Hastings, Charles Wilkins, and Sir William Jones—deeply admired and patronized ancient Sanskrit, Persian, and Arabic learning. Statement II is true: in his discourses to the Asiatic Society of Bengal, William Jones praised Indian civilization as equal to Europe in imagination, ratiocination, and philosophy.

items.title: Mock #06 · Q38
items.stem:
Place the following works in ascending order of their publication year.
A. Diamond Dust by Anita Desai
B. Breast-Giver by Mahashweta Devi
C. Death and the King’s Horseman by Wole Soyinka
D. Dream on Monkey Mountain by Derek Walcott
E. Exile and the Kingdom by Albert Camus
items.explanation: Arranging the works in ascending order of publication gives Albert Camus's Exile and the Kingdom (1957, E), Derek Walcott's Dream on Monkey Mountain (1970, D), Wole Soyinka's Death and the King's Horseman (1975, C), Mahasweta Devi's Breast-Giver (1977, B), and Anita Desai's Diamond Dust (2000, A), producing E-D-C-B-A.

items.title: Mock #06 · Q39
items.meta: Unit V: Language: Basic Concepts, Theories and Pedagogy
items.stem:
Which of the following definitions of linguistic terms are correct?
A. Orthoepy is the study of correct grammar in conformity with established regional patterns.
B. Philology is the study of phonemes and other characteristics of the systems of speech sounds in individual languages.
C. Synchronic study pertains to study of language at a specific historical point
D. Diachronic study pertains to historical dimensions of language i.e., linguistic change over the period of time.
E. Phonology is the study of language in its cultural and social contexts.
items.explanation: In modern linguistics, synchronic analysis examines a language's system at a particular fixed moment in time (C), while diachronic analysis investigates how languages evolve and change across historical time (D). Orthoepy is the study of correct pronunciation (not grammar), and phonology studies the sound systems of languages (whereas sociolinguistics examines social and cultural contexts).

items.title: Mock #06 · Q40
items.stem: Which among the following is not a play written by Eugene O'Neill?
items.explanation: The Plough and the Stars (1926), set during the 1916 Easter Rising in Dublin, was written by Irish dramatist Sean O'Casey. Anna Christie (1921), All God's Chillun Got Wings (1924), and Strange Interlude (1928) are plays by American playwright Eugene O'Neill.

items.title: Mock #06 · Q41
items.stem:
Below are two sets of texts one of which has inspired the other.  Match the text with its
inspiration :
(i)
Coral Island
(ii)
The Odyssey
(iii)
The Mahabharat
(iv)
Jane Eyre
(v)
The Great Indian Novel
(vi)
Wide Sargasso Sea
(vii)
Omeroos
(viii),Lord of the Flies
items.explanation: R. M. Ballantyne's The Coral Island inspired William Golding's Lord of the Flies; Homer's Odyssey inspired Derek Walcott's Omeros; the epic Mahabharata inspired Shashi Tharoor's The Great Indian Novel; and Charlotte Bronte's Jane Eyre inspired Jean Rhys's Wide Sargasso Sea.

items.title: Mock #06 · Q42
items.stem: Who among the following acknowledged that poetry is formed from the same elements as prose; the difference lies in the different combination of these elements and the difference of purpose?
items.explanation: In Chapter XIV of Biographia Literaria (1817), Samuel Taylor Coleridge states that poetry is composed of the same elements as prose composition, and that the difference consists in a different combination of them, in consequence of a different object proposed.

items.title: Mock #06 · Q43
items.stem:
Identify the two names from the following who are associated with Hermeneutics :
(a) Edmund Husserl
(b) E. D. Hirsch
(c) Martin Heidegger
(d) Stephen Greenblatt
Choose the correct option :
items.explanation: Hirsch ('Validity in Interpretation') and Heidegger are central to hermeneutics. Husserl is a phenomenologist and Greenblatt a New Historicist.

items.title: Mock #06 · Q44
items.stem: Which one of the following captures accurately the view of Frankfurt School of Critical Theory?
options: the culture industries instil in their mass audiences a capacity to question and transform
The analysis of culture should be divorced from politics and power relations
Power and culture are two distinct modes of social articulation, separate from each other
The culture industries engender passivity and conformity among their mass audiences
items.explanation: Adorno and Horkheimer argued that the culture industry makes audiences passive and conformist.

items.title: Mock #06 · Q45
items.stem:
Identify the correct chronological sequence of publication of the four parts of The Four
Quartets
options: Burnt Norton - The Dry Salvages - East Coker - Little Gidding
Burnt Norton - Little Gidding -The Dry Salvages - East Coker
Little Gidding - Burnt Norton - The Dry Salvages - East Coker
Burnt Norton - East Coker - The Dry Salvages - Little Gidding
items.explanation: The four poems comprising T. S. Eliot's Four Quartets (collected 1943) were originally published in the following chronological order: 'Burnt Norton' (1936), 'East Coker' (1940), 'The Dry Salvages' (1941), and 'Little Gidding' (1942).

items.title: Mock #06 · Q46
items.stem: Steeling herself to the murder, Lady Macbeth calls on ______ to "unsex me here". (Macbeth I.5.39) Choose the right option to fill in the blank
items.explanation: In Act I, Scene 5 of Shakespeare's Macbeth, after reading Macbeth's letter about the witches' prophecy, Lady Macbeth invokes demonic powers ('the spirits / That tend on mortal thoughts') to 'unsex me here, / And fill me from the crown to the toe top-full / Of direst cruelty!'

items.title: Mock #06 · Q47
items.stem:
Given below are two statements : One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion (A): Roland Barthes describes two basic categories of text as "the readerly" and "the writerly".
Reason (R): Language is the window through which one sees the world.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct

items.title: Mock #06 · Q57
items.stem: Which of the following assertions is/are not true in the context of culture industry? (A) The term 'culture industry' was used by the Frankfurt School to describe the operations of mass media. (B) The dominant capitalist class instils its values and beliefs in the minds of the working-class people. (C) The word 'industry' signifies the production of cultural products for mass consumption. items.explanation: In Dialectic of Enlightenment (1944), Theodor Adorno and Max Horkheimer argued that the culture industry commodifies culture into standardized products that generate mass deception, passive conformity, and ideological submission, actively eradicating authentic autonomous working-class culture (making D false) and suppressing critical thinking and activism (making E false).

items.explanation: Early plays by Harold Pinter—such as The Room (1957), The Birthday Party (1958), and The Dumb Waiter (1959)—were termed 'Comedies of Menace' by critic Irving Wardle. In Pinter's dramatic world, a pervasive,nameless dread and threat of intrusion hang in the air, yet the exact source or motive of the menace is never explicitly explained.

Bare.

items.explanation: The contrast between a luxurious "crystal stair" and stairs with tacks, splinters, torn-up boards, and bare wood signifies that the speaker's life has been filled with severe poverty, physical danger, and continuous racial struggle.

items.title: Mock #06 · Q93
items.stem:
[Reading Comprehension: Poem]
Read the following poem carefully and answer the question that follows:

"Mother to Son" by Langston Hughes

Well, son, I'll tell you:
Life for me ain't been no crystal stair.
It's had tacks in it,
And splinters,
And boards torn up,
And places with no carpet on the floor—
Bare.
But all the time
I'se been a-climbin' on,
And reachin' landin's,
And turnin' corners,
And sometimes goin' in the dark
Where there ain't been no light.
So boy, don't you turn back.
Don't you set down on the steps
'Cause you finds it's kinder hard.
Don't you fall now—
For I'se still goin', honey,
I'se still climbin',
And life for me ain't been no crystal stair.

Question:
Which rhetorical device has been used by the poet by repeating “And” at the beginning of – lines in the poem ?
items.explanation: Repeating the conjunction "And" at the beginning of successive poetic lines ("And splinters, / And boards torn up, / And places with no carpet...") is anaphora, which rhetorically emphasizes the relentless, accumulating obstacles in the speaker's climb.

[Reading Comprehension: Prose Passage]
Read the following passage carefully and answer the question that follows:

From "What is Art?" in Personality (1917) by Rabindranath Tagore

"Man also must know because he must live; and all the knowledge which is for his living comes under the category of science. But where he acquires a surplus of knowledge beyond the primary necessities of life, knowledge becomes freedom. Like a big merchant he can indulge in the luxury of having a wealth that has no direct bearing upon his life's necessities. It gives him the freedom to be useless and irresponsible. Animals are bound to their physical necessities and self-sustenance, while man alone seeks attainment of spiritual and creative freedom through knowledge and art." 

Question:
What does the author mean by “Man also must know because he must live” ?
options: Knowledge enables one to acquire wealth
Knowledge is the essence of man’s life
Knowledge is vital for countering animals
items.explanation: Tagore opens the passage by observing that knowledge essential for survival belongs to science, establishing that the acquisition of knowledge is fundamentally necessary to sustain human life and existence.
